prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Elements:
- aircraft (alias: Equipped aircraft, IFR aircraft) [first U0001]
- Traffic Flow Management (alias: TFM) [first U0001]
- Controlled Time of Arrival (alias: CTA) [first U0001]
- Management by Trajectory (alias: MBT) [first U0001]
- four-dimensional trajectories (alias: 4DTs, 4DT) [first U0001]
- Trajectory Based Operations (alias: TBO) [first U0013]
- Advanced Interval Management (alias: A-IM) [first U0067]
Earlier facts:
- flow(source=aircraft, target=Flight Management System, payload=trajectories) @U0070
- flow(source=controller, target=aircraft, payload=assigned trajectories) @U0068
- flow(source=controller, target=aircraft, payload=closed trajectories) @U0067
- action(performer=Traffic Flow Management, label=select more-effective TMIs) @U0098
- requirement(subject=Traffic Flow Management, text=Improved predictability resulting from MBT will allow TFM to select more-effective TMIs.) @U0098
- action(performer=aircraft, label=follow the assigned trajectories) @U0097
- action(performer=Management by Trajectory, label=addresses the satisfaction of the constraints) @U0097
- action(performer=Management by Trajectory, label=addresses the modification of assigned trajectories as constraints change) @U0097
- action(performer=Management by Trajectory, label=addresses the assignment of trajectories that are compliant with all TMIs) @U0097
- action(performer=Traffic Flow Management, label=selecting traffic management initiatives (TMIs)) @U0096
- requirement(subject=Management by Trajectory, text=Surface operations will be very diverse for different types of users, further motivating treating MBT ground operations as a separate research topic.) @U0092
- requirement(subject=Management by Trajectory, text=the application of MBT to surface operations will not be pursued in this effort unless the incremental benefits of including management of surface operations within the MBT concept is justified.) @U0086

Document units:
U0101: The operator will have flexibility to determine when the aircraft takes off, depending on how fast or slow it wants to fly to conform with the CTA and how the takeoff time will affect other constraints.
U0102: Mile-in-trail and minute-in-trail (MINIT) restrictions will be reduced in the near term and eventually eliminated as unnecessary when flights are following 4DTs that include time-based constraints where necessary.
U0103: Increased use of self-separation techniques (e.g., A-IM) will allow efficient management of aircraft merging to a runway or other constrained airspace resource, without needing to repeatedly update time constraints in the assigned trajectories in response to residual uncertainty.
U0104: By keeping all flights on closed trajectories that are de-conflicted over at least the next 30 minutes, MBT may increase sector capacities.
U0105: Uncertainty, which MBT will reduce, hampers current TFM performance.
U0106: However, many TFM processes take advantage of the flexibility in current operations.
U0107: In any TBO environment, if aircraft are more predictable and are scheduled accordingly, the reduction in uncertainty may be accompanied by a reduction in flexibility.
U0108: However, some residual uncertainty will persist, creating the possibility that the TFM system might be more fragile to the remaining uncertainty.
U0109: One area in which research will be required to validate the MBT concept is how TFM must adjust to the tradeoff between uncertainty and flexibility to achieve the anticipated TFM benefits.
U0110: For example, if TFM continues to be conservative and initially absorb less delay than it expects will be required, to leave flexibility to fill an empty slot caused by another flight being late, then most flights will need their assigned trajectories to be updated, potentially multiple times, as the TFM system “releases” more and more of the expected necessary delay to the flights.
